briefs.5993599385e99923: The question asks whether the first published FRED DGS10 value (10-year Treasury constant-maturity yield) for 2026-11-13 is above 4.86 percent; a print of exactly 4.86 does not count, and later revisions do not count (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10). The latest FRED observation is 4.86 percent for 2026-11-06, the same as the threshold, and the page was updated on 2026-11-09. The Treasury daily par yield curve row for 2026-11-09 shows a 10-year value of 4.88, with 4.86 for 2026-11-06 (https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value_month=202611, 2026-11-09); that table is a separate series from FRED's, so the two can differ by a basis point. The base rate was counted from the full FRED daily history: pairs of observations five trading days apart (the 2026-11-06 to 2026-11-13 gap) had the later value higher in 54.5 percent of the last 246 pairs, 53.7 percent of the last 1,244 pairs over five years, and 49.4 percent of the last 2,494 pairs over ten years. Moves of 0.02 points or more upward happened in 45.9 percent of the last-year pairs and moves of 0.02 or more downward in 32.5 percent. These shares measure direction, not the share of values above a fixed level. Two scheduled events fall in the window: the October 2026 CPI at 8:30 AM ET on 2026-11-10 (https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/cpi.htm) and a 42 billion dollar 10-year note auction at 1:00 PM ET the same day (https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0678, 2026-11-04). The Federal Reserve held its target range at 3-3/4 to 4 percent on 2026-10-28 with two members dissenting in favour of a quarter-point increase (https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20261028a.htm), and the next meeting is December 8-9, so no policy decision falls before resolution. No consensus forecast for the October CPI was found, and the September CPI was reported as 3.7 percent over 12 months. The case for a print at or below 4.86 rests on the tie rule and on any soft CPI or strong auction reaction. A hot CPI, given the two hawkish dissents, would push the yield above the line, and the number to watch is the DGS10 value published for 2026-11-10 to 2026-11-12 relative to 4.86.
